title: VESPER Checkpoint
description: IC-007. A checkpoint is a RESUMPTION RECORD, not a memory dump. It is what makes DR-007 ('tasks survive model/device transitions') and SR-060 (survival on a last-resort node) true rather than hoped for -- which is why it must stay small enough to carry to the weakest node in the fabric. Authority: DR-007, DR-017, RB-008, RB-026, RB-035, ARCH-03; REM-002, REM-014.

lease_epoch.description: Fencing: a checkpoint written under a stale epoch is not restorable as owner (INV-OWN-3).

goal.description: RB-029: refinable by evidence, but a resumed task may not silently become a different objective.

grant_refs.description: Grant REFERENCES ONLY. A checkpoint never carries grant secrets or credentials -- it travels to whichever node resumes the task, including a Z1 worker, and a secret in a checkpoint is a secret on every node that ever restores it.

outbox_cursor.description: INV-TASK-2. Resume replays from HERE, never from plan start. This single field is what prevents a node failover from re-sending an email that was already sent (A-034.5).

resource_consumed.description: Budgets are cumulative across resumption: a task cannot reset its own budget by being migrated (RB-018, RB-035).

survival_carry.description: SR-060 / INV-PLACE-3: whether this checkpoint is part of the core set carried onto a last-resort survival node. Task state is core; large derived artifacts are not.

$comment: EXCLUDED BY DESIGN: model context windows, raw media, secrets, and full retrieval results. A checkpoint that grows with conversation length cannot be carried to the weakest reachable node, which is precisely when it matters most.
